name: IN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 district with incumbent Rep. Jim Baird running for re-election
Baird's roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge plus $537K in outside support
Polymarket prices Democratic chances at just 3%
No public polling; challenger Drew Cox has only $6.8K on hand
model.rationale: The district's 15-point Republican lean, Baird's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and market pricing near 97% Republican all point the same way, and no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive race. A modestly favorable national environment for Democrats and about $200,000 in outside spending against Baird are the only counterweights, and they are not enough to close a double-digit gap.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending well beyond the $200,000 already deployed, or surprise polling showing a single-digit race, would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is a strongly Republican seat, and Rep. Jim Baird is seeking another term with the full advantage of incumbency in a district that backed Republicans by about 15 points at the presidential level. Challenger Drew Cox has raised roughly $61,000 and had under $7,000 on hand in the latest reporting, while Baird has raised about $605,000 and drawn more than $500,000 in outside support. Outside groups have also spent about $200,000 opposing Baird, a modest signal of Democratic interest in the seat.

No public polls of the race are available, and no major expert ratings list it as competitive. Prediction markets put Baird's chances near 97%. The forecast expects Baird to win by roughly 15 points, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling but not enough to make the outcome genuinely in doubt.
